freeze_note: This manifest freezes the tensor-network release protocol and records that its capacity premise is not yet established. Two earlier capacity candidates were falsified by measurement rather than by argument. First, flagquantum_18q_13l_expectation was frozen as the premise of an earlier campaign and then completed on a single A800 in 14.296 s at a 0.70 GiB peak, so it cannot be the workload one device fails to train. Second, the 24-qubit and 28-qubit grid ladder that replaced it does not separate the two cases either: the reverse-mode peak is not slice-owned above four sliced labels, so every measured shape that exhausts one device also exhausts both devices at the same peak. The ladder is recorded under capacity_workload.measured_ladder and capacity_workload.premise_established is false, because a premise declared rather than measured is not evidence. The gate therefore reports capacity_premise_not_established rather than passing on an assumed premise, and the capability stays at production_supported until a measured shape separates a single-device failure from a sharded completion. The speed protocol is frozen here so that the part of the release that does not depend on the premise can still be measured at one revision.

topologies.note: The measured cluster is one pair of hosts, so the release topology is a pair: two ranks, one device each, one on each host. No third host exists here, which is why the frozen topology is a pair rather than a ladder, and why the pair-only boundary is disclosed as a permanent limitation of the capability rather than as a stage of its measurement.

speed_workload.name: tensor_network_matched_speed_v1
speed_workload.timing_unit: one full forward-and-reverse training step over the sliced network
speed_workload.freeze_note: The timing protocol is two warmup and ten measured iterations rather than the statevector lane's five and thirty, because one tensor-network step is a complete forward and reverse contraction over the sliced network and takes orders of magnitude longer than one statevector training step at a comparable width. The protocol is frozen before the run and the acceptance configuration is the widest point of each frozen multiset.

capacity_workload.name: tensor_network_single_device_capacity_v1
capacity_workload.premise_established_note: A capacity premise requires one measured shape that exhausts a single device and that a sharded run completes. No such shape was measured on this pair. The reverse-mode peak fell from 80.93 GiB at two sliced labels to 51.19 GiB at four and then stopped responding to slicing, so the four-sliced-label 4x6x2 run completes on one device at 51.19 GiB and the same run completes across the pair at the same peak: the pair demonstrates a sharded training update, not capacity expansion.

single_gpu_baseline.rationale: The single-device capacity failure is read as provenance evidence rather than as a release-gate payload, for the same reason the statevector lane reads it that way: a single device cannot shard one logical workload across ranks, so no world_size 1 artifact can satisfy the release gate. It is read from results_path rather than from benchmarks/results/scalability because the strict promotion audit requires every file in that directory to be release-grade sharded scalability evidence.
